neighbours.label: descriptions of how a physical structure bears or cushions weight (mattress, bra, arches), where a word like 'support' is near
fire: Our hybrid mattress cradles your shoulders and keeps the lower back aligned through the night.
The orthopaedic insole lifts the heel and takes the load off the ball of your foot.
This sports bra has wide straps and firm cups that stay put while you run.
The nave roof is carried on pointed arches that spring from massive piers.
A steel lintel spans the opening and transfers the weight of the wall to the posts.
The ergonomic chair hugs the curve of your spine and eases pressure on the hips.
Flying buttresses brace the upper walls and carry the thrust of the vault to the ground.
Este colchón se adapta a tu espalda y alivia la presión en las caderas durante la noche.
quiet: Our mattress arrives in a blue box with a printed receipt and free delivery to your door.
The insole comes in six colours and ships from our warehouse in about two days.
This sports bra was named after a runner and costs less than last year's version.
The nave was painted in the 1800s by a local artist who loved the colour green.
A brass plaque beside the door records the name of the family who owned the house.
The office chair was on sale last week, so my sister bought one for her son.
Tourists photograph the cathedral at sunset and buy postcards from the kiosk on the square.
Este colchón llegó el martes en una caja azul y mi hermana pagó con tarjeta en la tienda.

notes: Card looks like Spanish function words, but its examples are arches, a pillow-top and a bra, and its output promotes ' support'. Probes: pillow-top 0.69, arches 0.55, columns 0.31, underwire 0.30, Spanish bra 0.21; novels in English or Spanish 0.00-0.04. Plain Spanish text is not enough, though Spanish church text gave 0.35.
